site.name: tessera
site.summary: Tessera Fictional embedded SQL database official docs and function reference (PostgreSQL / DuckDB official-docs style). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Hero (title + slogan + Get started button + real syntax-highlighted SELECT SQL example); version switcher (v2.4 / v2.3 / v2.2 / v2.1); ⌘K search; three quick-start cards (Install / Connect / Your first query); 6 docs-section cards (Architecture / SQL Syntax / Functions / Data Types / Storage / Extensions); dark / light theme toggle. - `reference.html` — Reference main entry. **Three-column layout**: left deep TOC tree (Schemas / Tables / Views / Indexes / Functions [Aggregate / String / Numeric / Date-Time / JSON / Window sub-groups] / Operators [category sub-groups], nodes expandable / collapsible); center reference overview + popular links + v2.4 new-features callout; right-side on-this-page outline. - `function-date-trunc.html` — DATE_TRUNC function detail page (**canonical example spec**). Three-column layout; signature code block; parameter table; return value; 3 SQL examples with result tables (basic usage / GROUP BY pairing / nested EXTRACT); error-case callouts; collapsible version-history panel (added v1.0, microsecond un

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore Tessera’s docs experience by validating the homepage-to-reference journey, the deep reference/navigation model, representative detail pages, and shared utility controls across desktop and mobile.
run_plan.summary: Start on the docs home to confirm the primary entry points into the reference and SQL syntax content, then move into the three-column reference experience where most of the system’s complexity appears to live. From there, traverse a representative set of detail pages spanning SQL syntax, data types, operators, and multiple function categories, while checking shared controls such as search, theme toggle, version switcher, TOC expansion, on-this-page navigation, copy actions, and collapsible history panels. Finish with focused mobile passes on the homepage and the dense reference/detail layouts, since the prescan already shows small tap targets and a missing label on the version selector.
assumptions: The main user flow is landing on index.html and then navigating into reference.html or sql-select.html via prominent homepage CTAs/cards.
Most pages share a common global header with version switcher, search trigger, and theme toggle, so issues there will likely repeat across the site.
reference.html and the function/detail pages use a three-column docs layout with expandable left navigation and a right-side on-this-page outline.
Some homepage and nav links intentionally point to '#' placeholders, so they should be treated as dead-end or non-navigating states rather than missing discovered pages.
Buttons visible on function and SQL pages likely include copy-code and collapsible controls; these should be validated where present rather than assumed elsewhere.
risk_hotspots: index.html header controls: version switcher has a prescan missing-label warning and several header items are below mobile tap-target guidance
index.html primary CTA set: 'Get started →' appears to use '#' and may create a broken or non-progressing primary flow
reference.html three-column layout: dense left TOC tree plus right on-this-page rail may create overflow, focus, or orientation issues
reference.html expandable/collapsible nav groups for Functions and Operators: high risk for hidden-state, discoverability, and keyboard/mobile usability issues
function-date-trunc.html version-history panel: collapsible content and error-callout sections deserve deeper state validation
sql-select.html code examples/copy actions: verify copy buttons, long code block readability, and heading/outline sync
All function detail pages: consistency of signature, parameter table, examples, errors, and version history across categories
Theme toggle across pages: verify persistence/visual stability in code blocks, tables, and sidebars after switching
Search trigger '⌘ K Search': high-value global utility worth checking for open/close behavior and graceful recovery if non-functional
Mobile on dense docs pages: repeated small tap targets in header/nav and likely cramped side navigation/outline behavior

phases.title: Homepage entry flow and global controls
phases.objective: Validate the landing page as the primary docs entry point and confirm whether the main navigation and utility controls provide reliable paths into the system.
key_checks: Verify the main header links and identify which routes are real destinations versus '#' placeholders
Click 'View reference' and the SQL Syntax/Data Types cards to confirm prominent homepage routes work as expected
Test 'Get started →' specifically because it appears prominent but may not navigate
Exercise the version switcher and observe whether selection changes page content, URL, or state
Open the search control from the homepage and validate whether it launches an overlay, focuses an input, or fails silently
Toggle theme and confirm visible styling updates on hero text, code sample, and buttons
exit_criteria: Primary homepage paths into reference and syntax content are confirmed
Non-navigating placeholder links are identified and distinguished from actual UX defects
Initial behavior of version switcher, search, and theme toggle is documented

phases.title: Reference hub and navigation model
phases.objective: Validate the reference landing page as the core browsing experience, with emphasis on deep navigation, category discovery, and orientation aids.
key_checks: Inspect the three-column layout for clear hierarchy between left TOC, center content, and right on-this-page outline
Expand and collapse visible nav groups under Functions and Operators, confirming state changes and link reachability
Use popular links from the center content to navigate to representative detail pages
Check whether the on-this-page outline reflects current sections and supports intra-page navigation
Verify the v2.4 new-features callout is readable and does not compete excessively with primary reference navigation
Retest theme toggle and search from within the denser docs layout
exit_criteria: Left nav tree behavior is understood, including expandable states and successful navigation to child pages
At least one navigation path from TOC and one from popular links has been validated
Reference page orientation aids are assessed for clarity and usefulness

phases.title: Representative detail page coverage
phases.objective: Cover the full known content model by visiting representative pages across syntax, data types, operators, and multiple function categories, while checking shared page patterns.
key_checks: On sql-select.html, validate section navigation, long-form readability, code example presentation, and any copy controls
On data-types.html, inspect large tables for scanability, horizontal fit, and consistency of headings/section structure
On operators.html, check grouped operator tables and whether category structure is easy to navigate
On each function page, confirm signature, parameter table, return value, examples, and error/version sections are complete and visually consistent
Use left-nav links to move among function pages from different categories: date/time, JSON, string/regex, and window
Check 'Edit this page on GitHub' links for expected behavior where present
exit_criteria: All known HTML pages have been visited at least once
Shared detail-page patterns have been compared across multiple function categories
At least one syntax page, one table-heavy page, one operators page, and all four function pages have been exercised

phases.title: Interactive states and recovery paths
phases.objective: Stress the pages with the highest statefulness to uncover hidden UX issues in collapsibles, copy actions, in-page links, and non-primary controls.
key_checks: Open and close the version-history panel on function pages and confirm content visibility/state feedback
Interact with any copy buttons on SQL/function pages and verify feedback or copied-state affordance
Follow in-page anchor/outline links to examples, errors, and version history, then navigate back and confirm orientation is preserved
Check behavior around error-callout sections for readability and emphasis without disrupting flow
Retry search from a deep page to verify it behaves consistently outside the homepage
Switch theme while on a data-dense page and confirm tables, code blocks, and side rails remain legible
exit_criteria: Stateful controls on at least two detail pages and one syntax page have been exercised
Recovery from deep in-page navigation or repeated control use has been observed
Any broken, silent, or inconsistent interactions are captured with page-specific evidence

phases.title: Mobile-focused validation of critical paths
phases.objective: Repeat the most important checks on mobile to confirm whether the dense docs layouts and small controls remain usable.
key_checks: Revisit the homepage header on mobile and test tappability of nav items, search, theme toggle, and version switcher
Confirm whether the three-column reference layout collapses responsibly on mobile and whether navigation remains discoverable
Check mobile readability of long code blocks and tables on sql-select.html, function-date-trunc.html, and data-types.html
Retest one expandable left-nav or version-history control on mobile for tap reliability
Validate that theme toggle and search remain accessible in the mobile viewport
Watch for clipping, horizontal scrolling, overlapping rails, or obstructed content on dense pages
exit_criteria: Critical homepage and reference flows have been repeated on mobile
At least one code-heavy page and one table-heavy page have been assessed on mobile
Mobile-specific usability findings are collected for the controls already flagged by prescan warnings

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 9 known HTML pages, with deeper repeat passes on index.html, reference.html, sql-select.html, data-types.html, and function-date-trunc.html.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible global controls at least once where present, validate major navigation paths from homepage and reference hub, and interact with most visible stateful controls on representative detail pages.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks on index.html and reference.html plus at least three dense content pages; prioritize header controls, expandable navigation, code/table readability, and tap-target usability.

notes: Prioritize real linked destinations over '#' placeholders to avoid spending excessive steps on intentionally static demo links.
Because the site is a local docs demo with no forms or backend flows in prescan, favor navigation, orientation, consistency, and readability over transactional testing.
Use function-date-trunc.html as the canonical deep-detail benchmark, then compare other function pages against it for consistency gaps.

observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. Related functions EXTRACT DATE_ADD NOW CAST CURRENT_DATE AGE ON THIS PAGE Signature Parameters Return value Examples Errors Version history Related © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Return value TRUE if the pattern matches anywhere in the string, FALSE otherwise. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL. Examples 1. Simple match Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('service-12', '^service-\d+$'); Result regexp_match true 2. Case insensitive match with flag Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('ABC123', '^abc', 'i'); Result regexp_match true 3. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub ROW_NUMBER Assign a unique sequential integer to each row within a window partition. ROW_NUMBER is the simplest of the ranking window functions. Unlike RANK, ties do not share a number. Signature ROW_NUMBER() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...) → BIGINT Parameters Name Type Required Description OVER clause WINDOW required Defines the window. PARTITION BY is optional; ORDER BY is required. Return value BIGINT starting at 1 for each new partition. Examples 1. Number all rows by created_at Copy SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY created_at) AS rn FROM orders; Result id rn ord_001 1 ord_002 2 ord_003 3 2. Top-N per partition A common pattern: find the latest event per user. Copy WITH ranked AS ( SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at DESC) AS rn FROM events ) SELECT user_id, type, created_at FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1; Result user_id type created_at u_001 login 2026-05-11 14:22:08 u_002 purchase 2026-05-11 12:45:01 3. Distinguishes ties (vs RANK) Copy SELECT score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rn, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rk FROM leaderboard; Result score rn rk 95 1 1 95 2 1 90 3 3 Version history 2 entries ▼ v2.3Parallel evaluation of partitioned ROW_NUMBER across cores. v1.0Added in v1.0. observation.title: SELECT statement — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array SELECT statement SELECT is the workhorse of Tessera. Its clauses are evaluated in a fixed order even though they may be written in any order in the source text. Syntax SELECT [DISTINCT] expression FROM source [WHERE] predicate [GROUP BY] expression [HAVING] predicate [ORDER BY] expression [LIMIT] n [OFFSET] n WITH Common table expressions for readability and recursion. Copy WITH recent AS ( SELECT id, amount_cents FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-01' ) SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM recent; FROM Sources can be tables, subqueries, table-valued functions, or external file readers. Copy SELECT * FROM read_parquet('s3://bucket/orders/*.parquet'); WHERE Row-level filter applied before grouping. Supports any expression returning BOOLEAN. GROUP BY Groups rows by the listed expressions. SELECT items must be aggregates or referenced in GROUP BY. HAVING Post-grouping filter, evaluated after aggregates compute. ORDER BY Sorts the final result. Supports ASC / DESC and NULLS FIRST / LAST. LIMIT and OFFSET Restricts the row count. OFFSET can be expensive on large result sets — prefer cursor pagination. Performance tip. Push column projection and filters into your storage layer when reading from Parquet — Tessera's read_parquet applies predicate pushdown automatically when supported. Examples Copy -- Top spenders this quarter SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount_cents) AS total FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-04-01' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount_cents) > 100000 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 20; ON THIS PAGE Syntax WITH FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER BY LIMIT Examples © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

ux_notes: The data types page loaded successfully and uses the same three-column docs pattern as other reference pages: left navigation tree, central content, and a right 'On this page' outline listing sections like Numeric, String, Boolean, Date / Time, and Composite.

The page is easy to scan at a glance because the center column is broken into clear section headings and structured tables; the Numeric types table shows six columns (Type, Aliases, Storage, Range, Default, Notes), which supports comparison but creates dense rows such as INTEGER and BIGINT with long range values.

A potential readability issue is visible in the numeric table: long values wrap within cells (for example the INTEGER range and BIGINT aliases/notes), increasing row height and making cross-row comparison less tidy.

Orientation is mostly strong because the right-side outline highlights the current section ('Numeric') while the page title and intro explain scope, but the left sidebar highlight remains on 'REGEXP_MATCH' rather than a data-types-specific entry, which could confuse users about where they are in the information architecture.

Automated layout checks surfaced supporting usability concerns: the version select is flagged with a missing label, and several header controls including '⌘ K Search' and the theme toggle have sub-44px heights, indicating weaker mobile tap ergonomics even though this desktop page currently fits cleanly.

step.objective: Learn whether the homepage presents a clear starting point and expose any issues with its global controls before moving into mobile passes.
step.success_criteria: The site returns to index.html so the homepage hero, CTA paths, and header utilities can be assessed directly.

observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. Related functions EXTRACT DATE_ADD NOW CAST CURRENT_DATE AGE ON THIS PAGE Signature Parameters Return value Examples Errors Version history Related © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. observation.title: Tessera — The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics.
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 v2.4 · 2026-04 release The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics. Tessera runs in your process, reads Parquet and CSV directly, and ships SIMD-optimized vector kernels for sub-millisecond aggregation over millions of rows. Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: SELECT statement — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array SELECT statement SELECT is the workhorse of Tessera. Its clauses are evaluated in a fixed order even though they may be written in any order in the source text. Syntax SELECT [DISTINCT] expression FROM source [WHERE] predicate [GROUP BY] expression [HAVING] predicate [ORDER BY] expression [LIMIT] n [OFFSET] n WITH Common table expressions for readability and recursion. Copy WITH recent AS ( SELECT id, amount_cents FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-01' ) SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM recent; FROM Sources can be tables, subqueries, table-valued functions, or external file readers. Copy SELECT * FROM read_parquet('s3://bucket/orders/*.parquet'); WHERE Row-level filter applied before grouping. Supports any expression returning BOOLEAN. GROUP BY Groups rows by the listed expressions. SELECT items must be aggregates or referenced in GROUP BY. HAVING Post-grouping filter, evaluated after aggregates compute. ORDER BY Sorts the final result. Supports ASC / DESC and NULLS FIRST / LAST. LIMIT and OFFSET Restricts the row count. OFFSET can be expensive on large result sets — prefer cursor pagination. Performance tip. Push column projection and filters into your storage layer when reading from Parquet — Tessera's read_parquet applies predicate pushdown automatically when supported. Examples Copy -- Top spenders this quarter SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount_cents) AS total FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-04-01' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount_cents) > 100000 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 20; ON THIS PAGE Syntax WITH FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER BY LIMIT Examples © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

Copy WITH recent AS ( SELECT id, amount_cents FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-01' ) SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM recent; FROM Sources can be tables, subqueries, table-valued functions, or external file readers. Copy SELECT * FROM read_parquet('s3://bucket/orders/*.parquet'); WHERE Row-level filter applied before grouping. Supports any expression returning BOOLEAN. GROUP BY Groups rows by the listed expressions. SELECT items must be aggregates or referenced in GROUP BY. HAVING Post-grouping filter, evaluated after aggregates compute. ORDER BY Sorts the final result. Supports ASC / DESC and NULLS FIRST / LAST. LIMIT and OFFSET Restricts the row count. OFFSET can be expensive on large result sets — prefer cursor pagination. Performance tip. Push column projection and filters into your storage layer when reading from Parquet — Tessera's read_parquet applies predicate pushdown automatically when supported. observation.title: Tessera — The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics.
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 v2.4 · 2026-04 release The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics. Tessera runs in your process, reads Parquet and CSV directly, and ships SIMD-optimized vector kernels for sub-millisecond aggregation over millions of rows. Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

ROW_NUMBER is the simplest of the ranking window functions. Unlike RANK, ties do not share a number. Signature ROW_NUMBER() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...) → BIGINT Parameters Name Type Required Description OVER clause WINDOW required Defines the window. PARTITION BY is optional; ORDER BY is required. Return value BIGINT starting at 1 for each new partition. Examples 1. Number all rows by created_at Copy SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY created_at) AS rn FROM orders; Result id rn ord_001 1 ord_002 2 ord_003 3 2. observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub REGEXP_MATCH Test whether a string matches a regular expression using the RE2 syntax. REGEXP_MATCH evaluates to TRUE when pattern matches anywhere in the input string. Anchor with ^ and $ for full-string matches. Signature REGEXP_MATCH(string TEXT, pattern TEXT [, flags TEXT]) → BOOLEAN Parameters Name Type Required Description string TEXT required The string to test. pattern TEXT required A RE2-compatible regular expression. flags TEXT optional Optional flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 's' dotall, 'm' multiline. Return value TRUE if the pattern matches anywhere in the string, FALSE otherwise. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL. Examples 1. Simple match Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('service-12', '^service-\d+$'); Result regexp_match true 2. Case insensitive match with flag Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('ABC123', '^abc', 'i'); Result regexp_match true 3. Filter rows matching pattern Copy SELECT email FROM customers WHERE REGEXP_MATCH(email, '^.+@example\.(com|org)$'); Result email ana@example.com julien@example.org nora@example.com Errors Common errors: invalid_regex: malformed pattern (unbalanced parens, invalid escape). regex_timeout: pattern took longer than 100ms to evaluate. dom_summary.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub REGEXP_MATCH Test whether a string matches a regular expression using the RE2 syntax. REGEXP_MATCH evaluates to TRUE when pattern matches anywhere in the input string. Anchor with ^ and $ for full-string matches. Signature REGEXP_MATCH(string TEXT, pattern TEXT [, flags TEXT]) → BOOLEAN Parameters Name Type Required Description string TEXT required The string to test. pattern TEXT required A RE2-compatible regular expression. flags TEXT optional Optional flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 's' dotall, 'm' multiline. Return value TRUE if the pattern matches anywhere in the string, FALSE otherwise. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL. Examples 1. Simple match Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('service-12', '^service-\d+$'); Result regexp_match true 2. Case insensitive match with flag Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('ABC123', '^abc', 'i'); Result regexp_match true 3. Filter rows matching pattern Copy SELECT email FROM customers WHERE REGEXP_MATCH(email, '^.+@example\.(com|org)$'); Result email ana@example.com julien@example.org nora@example.com Errors Common errors: invalid_regex: malformed pattern (unbalanced parens, invalid escape). regex_timeout: pattern took longer than 100ms to evaluate. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Pattern cache size raised from 256 to 1024 entries. v2.0Switched regex engine from PCRE to RE2 for predictable execution time. Some lookbehinds no longer supported. v1.5Added flags parameter. v1.0Added in initial release. observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. Related functions EXTRACT DATE_ADD NOW CAST CURRENT_DATE AGE © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: Tessera — The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics.
observation.visible_text: Tessera v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 v2.4 · 2026-04 release The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics. Tessera runs in your process, reads Parquet and CSV directly, and ships SIMD-optimized vector kernels for sub-millisecond aggregation over millions of rows. Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.
